exercises.name: Chin Tucks
exercises.form_cue: Sit tall. Draw chin straight back. Feel stretch at skull base. Weekly maintenance dose.
exercises.why: Minimum effective dose to maintain C5-6 decompression benefits during high running volume.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Flexion
exercises.form_cue: Press forehead into palm. Resist firmly. Hold 10 sec. Minimal maintenance.
exercises.why: Weekly minimum to preserve cervical strength gains.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Extension
exercises.form_cue: Press back of head into palm. Resist firmly. Hold 10 sec.
exercises.why: Weekly minimum to preserve posterior cervical strength.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Neck Flexion
exercises.form_cue: Anchor band behind head at eye level. Stand facing anchor. Place band around forehead. Nod chin to chest against band resistance. Controlled movement.
exercises.why: Maintenance dynamic resistance exercise to keep cervical flexors strong through running phase.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation
exercises.form_cue: Sit on chair, cross arms on chest. Rotate thoracic spine left and right. Full range. Weekly maintenance.
exercises.why: Maintenance thoracic mobility to support running posture at increasing intensities.

exercises.name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Tilt head away from tight side. Gentle hand overpressure. Both sides equally.
exercises.why: Flexibility maintenance during peak training volume.

exercises.name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Straighten left arm, palm down. Use right hand to gently press hand down. Weekly maintenance.
exercises.why: Minimum dose flexibility maintenance for the common extensor tendon.

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Extensions (Maintenance — 3-4kg)
exercises.form_cue: Rest forearm on table, wrist over edge, palm down. Hold 3-4kg dumbbell. Assist raising wrist up. Slowly lower under control (4-5 sec). Weekly maintenance.
exercises.why: Weekly heavy eccentric loading is the minimum dose to maintain tendon integrity during sustained running training.

exercises.name: Band Wrist Extensions
exercises.form_cue: Anchor resistance band under foot. Hold band end, palm down. Extend wrist up against band resistance. Controlled return.
exercises.why: Maintenance band loading for wrist extensor strength.

exercises.name: Grip Squeezes
exercises.form_cue: Squeeze a firm grip trainer. Hold 5 sec. Release. Maintenance dose.
exercises.why: Weekly grip strength maintenance for arm swing efficiency during runs.

exercises.name: Mountain Climbers
exercises.form_cue: Start in push-up position. Alternate driving knees toward chest rapidly. Keep hips down — don't let them rise. 30 reps = 15 each leg. Controlled rhythm.
exercises.why: Running-specific core exercise: mimics the hip flexion pattern and trunk stability demands of running. Builds dynamic core endurance.

exercises.name: Dead Bug with Band
exercises.form_cue: Lie on back. Loop resistance band around both feet. Arms point to ceiling holding band ends. Extend opposite arm and leg against band resistance. Keep lower back flat.
exercises.why: Band-resisted dead bugs are running-specific — the band mimics the hip flexor and shoulder forces encountered during running gait.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
exercises.form_cue: Lie on side. Place top foot on a bench/chair. Lift hips off floor — only the top foot and elbow contact surfaces. Body forms a straight line. Hold 20-30 sec each side.
exercises.why: Copenhagen plank is the gold standard running injury prevention exercise — dramatically reduces groin/adductor injuries in runners.

exercises.name: Plank with Shoulder Taps
exercises.form_cue: Start in high plank (hands). Lift one hand to tap opposite shoulder. Return. Alternate. Keep hips still — don't rock side to side.
exercises.why: Dynamic plank trains the anti-rotation stability required during running arm swing.

exercises.name: Anti-Rotation Press
exercises.form_cue: Stand sideways to band anchor. Hold band at chest. Press straight out, hold 2 sec, return. Heavier band than Phase 3. Both sides.
exercises.why: Maintenance and progression of anti-rotation strength for running efficiency.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Bridge March
exercises.form_cue: Single-leg bridge position. Maintain hips high and stable while slowly marching free leg. Simulate running hip flexion. 20 reps each side.
exercises.why: Running-specific: simulates the late stance/swing phase hip pattern under loaded conditions.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Squats (Pistol Prep)
exercises.form_cue: Stand on one leg near a wall for safety. Lower to 90° or deeper, keeping knee tracking over toes. Drive up through heel. Other leg extends forward. Use wall if needed.
exercises.why: Single-leg squat is the ultimate running strength test — mimics the force demands of each step. Prerequisite for injury-free 30-min running.

exercises.name: Plyometric Squat Jumps
exercises.form_cue: Stand feet shoulder-width. Squat down, then explode up. Land softly through toe-to-midfoot-to-heel. Absorb landing in squat position. Rest 10 sec between reps.
exercises.why: Plyometric loading prepares leg tendons and muscles for running impact forces. Reduces injury risk when volume increases.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hops (Forward)
exercises.form_cue: Stand on one leg. Hop forward, absorb landing on same leg. Hold 2 sec to demonstrate control. 8 hops each leg. Start small — quality over distance.
exercises.why: Direct plyometric preparation for running's single-leg loading pattern. Builds reactive calf and ankle stiffness.

exercises.name: Hill Sprint Preparation — Uphill Strides
exercises.form_cue: Find a gentle slope (5-8% grade). Run uphill at 80% effort for 20 sec. Walk back down fully. 4 repetitions. Focus on driving knees and pumping arms.
exercises.why: Uphill running reduces impact forces while building leg power and cardiovascular capacity — ideal progressive overload before flat-ground speed work.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raises — Heavy
exercises.form_cue: Hold heavy dumbbells (or use calf raise machine). Single-leg on step edge. Rise up fully, hold 2 sec, lower slowly (4 sec) below step. Full range of motion.
exercises.why: Phase 4 calf loading at 2-3x bodyweight equivalent prepares the Achilles for the 4x bodyweight demand of sustained running.

exercises.name: Goblet Squats — Heavy
exercises.form_cue: Hold heavy dumbbell or kettlebell at chest. Feet shoulder-width. Deep squat, elbows inside knees. Drive up through heels. Chest tall.
exercises.why: Heavy loaded squats maintain lower body strength during peak running volume.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Half-kneeling with overhead reach. Push hips forward, squeeze glute of back leg. Maintenance dose. Critical with high run volume.
exercises.why: Hip flexor flexibility maintenance is critical as run volume reaches 30+ min — prevents anterior pelvic tilt and back pain.
